summary: During the same meeting, Bjorn discovers that the room has firm participation rules without anyone commanding who must speak.
settingText: Same community-center multipurpose room during the first meeting.

panelPlan.action: A silence lasts without anyone rushing to fill it. Bjorn looks around the circle, trying to locate the person responsible for deciding who goes next.
The facilitator answers from the same kind of chair as everyone else, relaxed and unceremonial.
Bjorn leans slightly forward, genuinely testing the structure rather than mocking it.
Several participants remain physically relaxed: one drinks coffee, one looks down, another listens without preparing to speak. Nobody is compelled to perform.
Bjorn recognizes the distinction between a rule and an order. The facilitator lets the distinction stand without congratulating him.

dialogueInline.text: Then anyone may take the room.
Anyone may speak. Anyone may pass. Anyone may disagree. Anyone may leave a question unanswered.

summary: Bjorn correctly sees that another participant is not fine, but the facilitator stops him from turning that perception into permission to speak for them.
settingText: Same community-center multipurpose room, later in the first meeting.

panelPlan.action: Another participant describes a visibly unstable housing/family situation while keeping their body closed and insisting they can manage.
Bjorn's attention sharpens and he answers before the participant asks for anything.
The participant stiffens as Bjorn states what he thinks they are afraid of.
The facilitator raises one hand from their chair and cuts Bjorn off without standing over him.
The facilitator keeps the correction practical: Bjorn may be right, but the other participant did not ask him to make their truth public.

dialogueInline.text: It's fine. I can handle it.
You fear saying so because then someone may decide for you.
You may be. They still did not ask you to say it for them.
Then what use is seeing it?
Sometimes you wait to be asked.

directionInline: The unnamed participant is an ordinary adult and remains visually separate from the recurring 1987 Participant.

summary: After the meeting, Carrie sees that Bjorn intends to return because he leaves still arguing with the facilitator instead of dismissing the room.
settingText: Community-center hallway and front sidewalk immediately after the first meeting.

panelPlan.action: Carrie waits on a bench scrolling work messages. The meeting-room door opens and participants filter out normally.
Bjorn exits while facing backward toward the facilitator inside, continuing the argument as he walks.
Carrie falls into step beside Bjorn and hides how interested she is in the fact that he is still engaged.
Bjorn and Carrie keep walking. The facilitator remains in the doorway and calls after him; Bjorn answers without turning back.

dialogueInline.text: If a man sees a roof falling, he does not wait for permission.

summary: At home, Bjorn nearly settles an argument between the two male Kin, stops himself, and asks whether they want his decision or only his judgment.
settingText: Safe Cave, afternoon: tool storage area and lease-painted wall.

panelPlan.location: Safe Cave wall and freestanding shelf
panelPlan.action: First Male Kin holds a small wooden tool rack against the painted wall while Second Male Kin points toward the freestanding shelf instead. A drill and small hardware sit nearby.
Bjorn enters, reads the disagreement instantly and raises one hand to settle it by habit.
He stops in the middle of the first word and lowers the hand slightly.
Bjorn asks what role they actually want from him. The two men exchange a quick look before First Male Kin answers.
Bjorn compares the landlord-painted drywall, the rack and the freestanding shelf before giving a narrow opinion. Second Male Kin sets the drill down rather than being ordered to do so.

dialogueInline.text: Do you ask for decision, or judgment?
Then do not put holes in another man's wall when a shelf will hold the same iron.

directionInline: Show exactly the two established male Kin. Astrid is absent; do not add a third Kin.

summary: Outside the bodega, Bjorn visibly waits through a delivery problem until the owner asks him to move one specific sack.
settingText: Bodega sidewalk and front aisle during a daytime delivery.

panelPlan.action: A delivery truck has left heavy sacks and cases on the sidewalk. The Bodega Owner and delivery worker sort them into a workable order.
Bjorn approaches and stops one full stride short of the work. His posture shows the impulse to step in, but he does not.
Bjorn's hand flexes once and relaxes at his side. No one has asked him for anything.
The owner looks up and points to one flour sack.
Bjorn carries exactly that sack inside and stops at the exact place the owner points to, then releases it.

dialogueInline.text: Bjorn. Grab that flour bag. Just that one.

summary: One male Kin repairs a loose stool and gives Bjorn the smaller job of holding a brace steady instead of surrendering the tools.
settingText: Safe Cave kitchenette, daytime, around a cheap modern stool and small hand tools.

panelPlan.action: A cheap modern stool has a loose cross-brace. Second Male Kin has a screwdriver and small clamp laid out for a practical repair.
Bjorn kneels beside him and reaches for the screwdriver as if taking over is the natural form of help.
Second Male Kin keeps the screwdriver and points to the loose brace instead.
Bjorn's large hands hold the brace perfectly straight while Second Male Kin tightens the screw himself.
Second Male Kin tests the repaired stool; it holds. Bjorn looks from the stool to his now-empty hands and is quietly satisfied.

directionInline: Only Second Male Kin is visible among the Kin. Astrid and First Male Kin are off-page.
